name: Middlesbrough
title: Middlesbrough Quiz with Answers — Boro Trivia
description: A Middlesbrough quiz with answers: Juninho, Ravanelli, the 2004 League Cup, the 2006 UEFA Cup run and the Riverside. Instant scoring, no sign-up.
intro: Some clubs give you trophies. Boro gave you a decade you couldn't look away from — Juninho arriving from São Paulo in October 1995 for around £4.75m, Fabrizio Ravanelli scoring a hat-trick on his debut in a 3-3 draw with Liverpool, and a three-point deduction for the unfulfilled trip to Blackburn that sent the club down in 1996-97 after two cup finals in the same season. This quiz lives in that territory: the names, the transfers and the afternoons Teesside still argues about.

Start earlier if you like. Middlesbrough were formed in 1876 by members of Middlesbrough Cricket Club looking for something to keep them fit through the winter, and the club's modern story starts in 1986, when a consortium including Steve Gibson saved it from liquidation and Bruce Rioch — working without pay through the crisis — took a young side from the Third Division to the First in successive promotions in 1987 and 1988. Ayresome Park was home for 92 years before the move to the Riverside in 1995, where Craig Hignett scored the new ground's first goal in a 2-0 win over Chelsea.

Then the reward. The 2004 League Cup, beaten finalists Bolton Wanderers swept aside inside seven minutes at the Millennium Stadium, was the first major trophy in the club's history, and captain Gareth Southgate went from lifting it to managing the club in 2006 on special dispensation without a Pro Licence. Two seasons later came the run nobody scripts: three goals down on aggregate against Basel, then again against Steaua Bucharest, and Massimo Maccarone scoring the decisive late goal in both.

The questions are drawn fresh each time, so a second go isn't the same round. Answers come with a line of context — where the fee went, who scored, what it cost — which is usually where the argument starts. Play it on the bus, play it against a mate, and see how much of the Robson era you actually kept.

faq.q: How well do you know Middlesbrough?
faq.a: This quiz is a decent test. It covers the 1876 formation by members of Middlesbrough Cricket Club, the 1986 rescue and the Rioch promotions, the Bryan Robson years, the 2004 League Cup and the 2005-06 UEFA Cup run. Every answer comes with a short explanation, so you pick things up even on the ones you miss.

faq.q: When did Middlesbrough win their first major trophy?
faq.a: The 2004 League Cup. Boro beat Bolton Wanderers 2-1 at the Millennium Stadium, with Joseph-Desire Job and Boudewijn Zenden scoring inside the first seven minutes and Kevin Davies pulling one back after a Mark Schwarzer error. It was the first major trophy in the club's history.

faq.q: Which players does the Middlesbrough quiz cover?
faq.a: Mostly the ones fans still name first: Juninho, who had three separate spells after his 1995 move from São Paulo; Fabrizio Ravanelli, signed from Juventus in 1996; Emerson, Alen Boksic, Gaizka Mendieta, Massimo Maccarone, Bernie Slaven, Craig Hignett, Paul Gascoigne and Mark Schwarzer, who stayed 11 years from 1997.

A three-point deduction. Boro called off a December Premier League fixture at Blackburn Rovers citing an injury and illness crisis, and the appeal against the penalty failed. Without the deduction they would have stayed up — in a season that also brought the FA Cup final defeat to Chelsea and the League Cup final replay loss to Leicester.
